official.deadline_central_display: 2026 cohort: applications accepted until 12 June 2026; the application portal reopens in November 2026 for the 2027 cohort (no exact 2027 deadline date published)
official.deadline_note: Master's admission windows at HSG run 1 October - 31 March or 1 October - 30 April depending on the programme (Joint Medical Master: 1 January - 30 April); Best Talents itself can only be applied for after admission to a specific Master's programme is confirmed. Decisions for the 2026 cohort were communicated by 12 July 2026 at the latest.
official.application_cycle: 2027 cohort application cycle (portal reopens November 2026); the 2026 cohort closed on 12 June 2026
official.status_note: The official page states 'Application portal is closed'. Applications for the 2026 cohort were accepted until 12 June 2026; the application portal reopens in November 2026 for the 2027 cohort.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Coverage of tuition fees (HSG Best Talents page). The HSG Foundation describes the per-talent package as up to CHF 10'000 for tuition fees, framed as a scholarship up to the amount of the scholar's tuition fees.
benefits: Financial support: Coverage of tuition fees and contributions to living expenses
Personal development: accompanying support programme as well as access to the HSG community with its lecturers, alumni and partner organisations
Early access to the network of the University, HSG Alumni and funding partners, and to personalities from business and society
Membership of the Best Talents peer group
eligibility: EU/EFTA nationals or holders of the Swiss C permit who are admitted to a Master's programme at HSG
A proven sense of responsibility towards society, the economy and the environment, and a diversity of perspectives
Expectation that Best Talents promote and support future Best Talents after completing their studies, in the spirit of a strong alumni community
requirements: Confirmed admission to HSG and to a specific Master's programme before applying
Submission of the additional application documents through the Best Talents portal
Recommended English of at least C1 according to the CEFR at the start of studies for English-taught programmes; no proof required at application
Evidence of engagement beyond studies, as the selection process looks for demonstrated involvement and responsibility
documents: The additional application documents submitted through the Best Talents portal after admission is confirmed; the public page does not publish an itemised list
selection_criteria: Proven sense of responsibility towards society, the economy and the environment
Selection by a qualified, independent and diverse committee together with the Master programmes; awards are made on an ongoing basis
coverage: Coverage of tuition fees and contributions to living expenses (HSG Best Talents page)

HSG Foundation per-talent package: up to CHF 10'000 for tuition fees, around CHF 10'000 for living costs, and up to CHF 5'000 for extracurricular support and development measures, totalling around CHF 25'000 per talent over the programme's three semesters
All programme management costs are carried entirely by the University of St.Gallen
application_method: Once admission to HSG and a specific Master's programme has been confirmed, select 'Apply now!' on the HSG Best Talents page
Submit the additional application documents through the portal
The Master programmes and a qualified, independent and diverse committee select the cohort; awards are made on an ongoing basis
official.application_route: Apply through the 'Apply now!' portal on the HSG Best Talents page once master's admission is confirmed; there is no separate application route for the Starr-funded awards
official.citizenship_residency: EU/EFTA nationals or holders of the Swiss C permit
official.international_eligibility: Only EU/EFTA nationals and holders of the Swiss C permit are eligible under the published rules; third-country nationals are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction published; open to students admitted to any HSG Master's programme
official.duration: Master's programme at HSG; the HSG Foundation frames the funding basis as three semesters, with the living-cost contribution stated over a 2-4 semester programme
official.description: The Starr International Foundation promotes education in Switzerland and abroad, and the HSG Starr International Foundation Fund supports excellence scholarships of the HSG Best Talents Programme. Best Talents offers financial support, including coverage of tuition fees and contributions to living expenses, together with a personal development programme for outstanding and engaged bachelor's graduates from EU/EFTA countries or holders of the Swiss C permit who are admitted to a master's at HSG.
official.region: Europe (EU/EFTA nationals and Swiss C permit holders)
official.program_type: Foundation-funded master's excellence scholarship, delivered through the HSG Best Talents Programme
official.english_requirement: No proof of language proficiency required at application; the recommended level at the start of studies is at least C1 according to the CEFR (published on the master's admission pages for English-taught programmes)

not_confirmed: itemised document list for the portal
verification.notes: The old dedicated Starr page (HTTP 404) no longer exists; the surviving official Starr statement is the unisg.ch 'Our donors' page, which routes the HSG Starr International Foundation Fund into the HSG Best Talents Programme. The published CHF figures come from the official HSG Foundation and describe the Best Talents package generally, not a Starr-specific amount, so no award amount is asserted.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no longer a standalone Starr scholarship: the Starr International Foundation fund now pays for places inside HSG's Best Talents Programme, so you must first win a master's place at St. Gallen and then compete for one of up to 45 funded slots per cohort. The award covers your master's tuition fees and adds a living contribution of around CHF 10,000 plus up to CHF 5,000 for extracurricular development across a three-semester programme. It is restricted to EU/EFTA nationals and Swiss C-permit holders, which excludes third-country applicants who tend to assume HSG master's scholarships are open to everyone. The 2026 window closed on 12 June 2026 and the portal reopens in November 2026 for the 2027 cohort, so build your extracurricular profile now rather than waiting for the portal.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Top-graded EU/EFTA or Swiss C-permit graduates with a strong record of civic, social or economic engagement who have already been admitted to an HSG master's programme
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your HSG master's admission first: Best Talents only opens to admitted students
Be ready when the portal reopens in November 2026 for the 2027 cohort, because awards are made on an ongoing basis and early complete submissions matter
Document your engagement with concrete roles and impact: student government, association boards, St. Gallen Symposium or START Summit volunteering, social or environmental initiatives
Reach C1 English before studies start; no certificate is needed at application, but the selection interview will expose weak language skills
Line up referees and project evidence early so the portal's required documents do not arrive half-finished
common_rejection_risks: Applying before the master's admission decision is confirmed - the portal is only for admitted students
Relying on grades alone: the programme explicitly looks for demonstrated engagement and responsibility beyond studies
Submitting late in an 'ongoing' round and finding the cohort has already filled
Third-country nationals applying under the old rules, which no longer match the fund's published eligibility
Submitting generic documents that show no sense of responsibility towards society, the economy or the environment
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Semester contributions and student fees, health insurance, and visa or residence costs for non-Swiss nationals, plus any living costs beyond the roughly CHF 10,000 living contribution and any travel or installation costs, which the published award wording does not cover
document_audit: The public Best Talents page mentions only 'additional application documents' without listing them, so check the portal fields the moment it opens and do not assume the upload set from a previous cycle still applies
For the underlying master's admission, credentials not issued in German, French, Italian or English require certified translations, and the CV template must be completed in English
Engagement evidence should carry dates and roles; undated membership lists are weak proof in a committee review
alerts: The dedicated 'Starr International Foundation Scholarship' URL is dead (HTTP 404), so any application through it is impossible; the live route is the HSG Best Talents page
The 2026 cohort closed on 12 June 2026 with decisions only final by 12 July 2026, so keep a funding backup until a decision arrives
Eligibility moved from holders of recognised foreign bachelor's degrees to EU/EFTA nationals and Swiss C-permit holders, so older advice about this scholarship circulating online is wrong
The fund now overlaps heavily with the general Best Talents award; expect competition across all 14 HSG master's programmes, not a separate Starr pool
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Win a master's place at HSG, wait for the November 2026 portal reopening, submit the additional documents through 'Apply now!', then pass the programme-and-committee review, with awards issued on an ongoing basis
